title: Determination of dimensions of exfoliating materials in aqueous suspensions
author: Karpovich, Vlasova, et al.

steps.title: Prepare Laponite dispersion
steps.instruction: Slowly add 0.1 g Laponite RD (BYK Additives & Instruments) to 20 mL deionized water whose pH has been adjusted to 10 with 1 M NaOH, stir the mixture for 45 min at 1000 rpm with a magnetic mixer, filter the suspension through a Whatman syringe filter (0.1 µm pore size) and let the resulting 0.5 w/v % dispersion age for 1 day before use.

steps.title: Measure particle size distribution by DLS
steps.instruction: Using a Malvern Zetasizer Nano ZS, set the back‑scattering angle to 175° and the laser wavelength to 632.8 nm; acquire the autocorrelation function and process it with the cumulant method. Record several number‑particle‑size distributions, calculate esd50 and esd84 for each, and average them (average esd50 = 14 nm, average esd84 = 18.4 nm).

steps.title: Measure NMR relaxation times
steps.instruction: With an Acorn Area particle analyzer (Xigo Nanotools) operating at 13.0 MHz, determine the spin‑lattice (T1) and spin‑spin (T2) relaxation times of hydrogen protons in (i) Laponite‑free water (Tf1 = 2.82 s, Tf2 = 2.63 s) and (ii) the 0.5 w/v % Laponite dispersion (T1 = 2.58 s, T2 = 1.09 s).

steps.title: Determine Tbi/εl – method 1 (bound water on powder)
steps.instruction: Degas Laponite powder for 5 h at 350 °C, then expose the dried powder in a sealed container to moist air for varying times to adsorb different water amounts; transfer the wetted powder to an NMR tube and measure T1 in the relaxometer. Calculate the adsorbed water mass from the difference between wet and degassed dry powders, plot T1 versus water weight fraction, locate the inflection point (Tb1 = 10.5 ms). Compute ε using α = 0.7 nm⁻² and RNa = 0.21 nm (ε = α π RNa² = 0.097) and use the bound‑water layer thickness l = 1 nm to obtain Tb1/εl = 0.108 s nm⁻¹.

substeps.instruction: Expose to moist air for set periods, then load into NMR tube.
Measure T1 for each hydration level.
Determine adsorbed water mass by weighing wet vs dry powder.
Plot T1 vs water weight fraction and find inflection point (Tb1 = 10.5 ms).
Use l = 1 nm to compute Tb1/εl = 0.108 s nm⁻¹.

steps.title: Determine Tbi/εl – method 2 (calibration sample)
steps.instruction: Prepare a 0.1 w/v % Laponite suspension aged 7 days (fully exfoliated), dilute it to 0.001 % concentration, deposit 10 µL of the dilute suspension onto a 1 cm² mica substrate and dry at 150 °C. Prior to AFM measurement, place the substrate in water vapor for 1 h and dry again. Measure particle diameter and thickness by tapping‑mode AFM (NTEGRA Aura, NT‑MDT): average diameter = 19 nm, thickness = 1.05 nm. From these data calculate the specific surface area Sc = 840 m² g⁻¹. Measure the spin‑spin relaxation time of this calibration sample (Tc2 = 1.90 ms) and compute Tb2/εl using Eq. (3), obtaining Tb2/εl = 5.7 × 10⁻³ s nm⁻¹.

substeps.instruction: Make 0.1 w/v % Laponite suspension, age 7 days.
Dilute to 0.001 % and pipette 10 µL onto 1 cm² mica.
Dry at 150 °C, then expose to water vapor for 1 h and dry.
Perform AFM (tapping mode) to obtain average diameter = 19 nm and thickness = 1.05 nm.
Calculate Sc = 840 m² g⁻¹ from AFM dimensions.
Measure Tc2 = 1.90 ms for the calibration sample.
Apply Eq. (3) to obtain Tb2/εl = 5.7 × 10⁻³ s nm⁻¹.

steps.title: Calculate specific surface area of dispersion
steps.instruction: Insert the measured relaxation times and the appropriate Tb/εl values into Eq. (2): using T1, Tf1 and Tb1/εl (method 1) yields S ≈ 710 m² g⁻¹; using T2, Tf2 and Tb2/εl (method 2) yields S ≈ 620 m² g⁻¹ for the 1‑day‑old dispersion.

steps.title: Calculate particle dimensions
steps.instruction: With the specific surface area (S) obtained above and the DLS‑derived esd50 = 14 nm and esd84 = 18.4 nm, solve the system of equations (1) for lateral size d and thickness t. Use the values from method 2 (more accurate) for the final reported dimensions; note that the calculated thickness is larger than the nominal 1 nm platelet thickness, indicating incomplete exfoliation in the 1‑day‑old sample.
